sections.overview: The Pawpaw Sphinx is an eastern North American hawkmoth; Hartweg’s Sphinx, Dolbogene hartwegii, is another sphingid in a separate genus.
sections.identification: Adults have dark brown forewings dusted with pale scales and span about 50–68 mm.
sections.habitat: The species ranges from southeastern Canada through the eastern United States, south to Florida and eastern Texas.
sections.diet: Caterpillars use pawpaw, sweetfern, alder and deciduous hollies; adults take nectar from flowers.
sections.behavior: Several broods occur along the Gulf Coast, while farther north the species generally has one annual brood.
sections.reproduction: Mature caterpillars pupate in underground burrows and overwinter there.
sections.ecology: Its larvae feed on several native woody plants, with pawpaw among the best-known hosts.
sections.conservation: The North American species account rates it G5, globally secure.
